From 9430ff992644e9f9c3ba6283cc56d40b421522e9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2019 20:06:09 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] sctp: fix ignoring asoc_id for tcp-style sockets on
 SCTP_ENABLE_STREAM_RESET sockopt

A similar fix as Patch "sctp: fix ignoring asoc_id for tcp-style sockets on
SCTP_DEFAULT_SEND_PARAM sockopt" on SCTP_ENABLE_STREAM_RESET sockopt.

Fixes: 99a62135e127 ("sctp: use SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC and add SCTP_CURRENT_ASSOC for SCTP_ENABLE_STREAM_RESET sockopt")
Signed-off-by: Xin Long <lucien.xin@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/sctp/socket.c b/net/sctp/socket.c
index 238e5c804cc9..6b0ee8946bdb 100644
--- a/net/sctp/socket.c
+++ b/net/sctp/socket.c
@@ -4281,6 +4281,9 @@ static int sctp_setsockopt_enable_strreset(struct sock *sk,
 		goto out;
 	}
 
+	if (sctp_style(sk, TCP))
+		params.assoc_id = SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC;
+
 	if (params.assoc_id == SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC ||
 	    params.assoc_id == SCTP_ALL_ASSOC)
 		ep->strreset_enable = params.assoc_value;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/sctp/socket.c`**
- Added a conditional check to determine if the socket style is TCP (`sctp_style(sk, TCP)`).
- If the socket style is TCP, the `assoc_id` in the `params` structure is set to `SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC`.

### Relationships
The modification in `net/sctp/socket.c` addresses a bug related to the handling of the `assoc_id` for TCP-style sockets when setting the socket option `SCTP_ENABLE_STREAM_RESET`. This change is similar to a previous fix made for the `SCTP_DEFAULT_SEND_PARAM` socket option, ensuring that the association ID is correctly recognized and utilized for TCP-style sockets in the context of stream reset functionality. The patch aims to enhance the behavior of SCTP (Stream Control Transmission Protocol) by ensuring that the correct association ID is applied, thereby fixing the issue of it being ignored.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
asoc = sctp_id2assoc(sk, params.assoc_id);
if (!asoc && params.assoc_id > SCTP_ALL_ASSOC &&
    sctp_style(sk, UDP))
    goto out;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `assoc_id` is not properly assigned for TCP-style sockets when the `SCTP_ENABLE_STREAM_RESET` socket option is set. The code checks for an association using `sctp_id2assoc`, and if it does not find a valid association (`asoc` is NULL) and the `assoc_id` is greater than `SCTP_ALL_ASSOC`, it incorrectly skips the handling of the `assoc_id` for TCP-style sockets, leading to it being ignored.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (sctp_style(sk, TCP))
    params.assoc_id = SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC;
```
Reason:
This line of code ensures that if the socket style is TCP, the `assoc_id` is explicitly set to `SCTP_FUTURE_ASSOC`. This assignment allows the code to correctly handle the stream reset option for TCP-style sockets, ensuring that the association ID is not ignored and that the stream reset functionality works as intended.
